subtitle: יוּד הַקְּטַנָּה וְהַקְּרִיאָה שֶׁל כּוֹרֶשׁ מֶלֶךְ פָּרַס
blurb: בַּמִּלָּה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁל הַתַּנַ״ךְ גָּרָה יוּד. הָעָם עוֹלֶה לִירוּשָׁלַיִם — וְיוּד יוֹצֵאת לַדֶּרֶךְ אֲחוֹרָה, עַד הַהַתְחָלָה.

artDirection.styleBlock: STYLE (identical opening for every prompt): elegant bohemian-chic enchanted picture-book world; flat matte gouache on warm textured paper, visible dry-brush grain; fine hand-drawn gold line accents; ancient Near-Eastern and Egyptian graphic-relief stylization (profile figures, frieze rhythm, flat stacked space); fairy-light glows; childlike yet luxurious; generous negative space; restrained, Klassen/Shulevitz-like composition.
artDirection.characterRule: YUD: a tiny deep-navy (#14213D) character shaped exactly like the Hebrew letter yud - a rounded head with a short tail curving down to the lower-left; two white dot eyes; NO arms, NO legs, NO mouth; she grips or waves with her tail only; emotion shown ONLY by eye shape; thin pale ivory outline so she reads on dark grounds; never smaller than 6% of image height. Render the background without her if layering (she is composited as a separate layer from the reference).
artDirection.colorScript: pp.1-5 night-blue exile (lapis #1F3A6E, midnight #14213D, ivory #F3E7D0 accents) -> p.6-7 first big gold (glazed mustard #D9A441, line gold #C9A24B) -> pp.8-12 terracotta/sand road (#C4623D, sand, dusty rose, olive shadows) -> pp.13-16 golden dawn over pale limestone.
artDirection.signatureMotifs: (1) gold palmette-lotus band as a thin border; (2) the white 'point of light' hidden on every page (lamp, glint, star, bead) - a find-it game; (3) the palm-arch, dark blue in exile, turning gold on the road. The gold thread always runs left-to-right (backward through the book); the caravan always moves right-to-left (forward).
artDirection.negativeBase: no text, no letters, no writing, no numerals, no idols or statues, no winged disc, no Marduk dragon (mushhushshu), no eight-pointed Ishtar star, no lamassu, no Eye of Horus, no ankh, no scarab, no depiction of God or divine figures, no beams-from-heaven cliché, no domes, no minarets, no turbans-with-jewels 'Arabian nights' costume, no pharaoh costumes, no bare shoulders or immodest dress, no photorealism, no 3D render, no glossy gradients

pages.text: בַּמִּלָּה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁל הַתַּנַ״ךְ גָּרָה יוּד, הָאוֹת הַכִּי קְטַנָּה.
pages.source: דברי הימים ב לו, כג (המילה האחרונה: "וְיָעַל"); סדר הספרים: בבא בתרא יד ע"ב
pages.illustration: WIDE, very quiet opening. Color-script: night-blue exile (lapis #1F3A6E into midnight #14213D at the edges). Composition: a vast unrolled scroll seen from slightly above, running off both page edges like a landscape; its 'writing' is only rows of soft abstract ivory dashes that fade toward the RIGHT (the long past of the book). At the far LEFT end of the very last row, one small warm glow - the last word. Yud sits inside that glow, lower-left third, at 7-8% of image height, eyes round and calm (content, at home). Scale contrast: the scroll is an endless terrain, Yud is a speck of life. The white 'point of light' motif = the glow itself. Gold palmette-lotus band as a thin border along the bottom edge only. Empty text-space: the entire upper 40%, deep blue paper with a faint gold star-dust. Mood: hush, a lullaby before the story. AVOID: legible letters or pseudo-Hebrew in the dashes, book-of-spells magic sparkles overload, a modern codex/book shape, no text, no letters, no writing, no numerals, no idols or statues, no winged disc, no Marduk dragon (mushhushshu), no eight-pointed Ishtar star, no lamassu, no Eye of Horus, no ankh, no scarab, no depiction of God or divine figures, no beams-from-heaven cliché, no domes, no minarets, no turbans-with-jewels 'Arabian nights' costume, no pharaoh costumes, no bare shoulders or immodest dress, no photorealism, no 3D render, no glossy gradients.
pages.page_turn: פתיחה שקטה וחשוכה - הדף הבא נפתח על עולם שלם שמסביב למגילה: בבל בלילה.

pages.text: "עַל נַהֲרוֹת בָּבֶל, שָׁם יָשַׁבְנוּ, גַּם בָּכִינוּ, בְּזָכְרֵנוּ אֶת צִיּוֹן."
pages.illustration: WIDE, low horizon. Color-script: night-blue exile, the deepest page of the book. A broad Babylonian canal flowing horizontally across the lower third, still water reflecting a thin crescent moon. On the far bank, a long low wall of Neo-Babylonian glazed lapis brick with a frieze band of simple palmettes (no animals), and beyond it a distant stepped silhouette of the city (no ziggurat shrine, no statues) - all flat, dark, monumental. On the near bank: a row of seated Judean exiles in profile, frieze-like, small against the scale of the city - wrapped headcloths, long tunics and mantles with sashes, women with long veils, children leaning on parents; postures heavy, heads bowed or turned toward the LEFT (west, toward Zion). Tall poplars ('aravim') lean over the water. Yud: on a low branch of the nearest poplar, upper-right of the figures, 6-7% height, eyes drawn as soft downward crescents (sad, listening). The 'point of light': one tiny clay oil lamp with a pinched spout glowing on the bank. Palm-arch motif: two date palms bending into a dark-blue arch framing the scene. Empty text-space: upper 35% night sky, clear of branches. AVOID: tears drawn as big cartoon drops, chains or captivity violence, Ishtar Gate lions or dragons, no text, no letters, no writing, no numerals, no idols or statues, no winged disc, no Marduk dragon (mushhushshu), no eight-pointed Ishtar star, no lamassu, no Eye of Horus, no ankh, no scarab, no depiction of God or divine figures, no beams-from-heaven cliché, no domes, no minarets, no turbans-with-jewels 'Arabian nights' costume, no pharaoh costumes, no bare shoulders or immodest dress, no photorealism, no 3D render, no glossy gradients.
pages.page_turn: מהרחב אל הקרוב: הדף הבא מתקרב אל ענף אחד ואל כינור אחד.

pages.text: שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה שָׁתְקוּ הַכִּנּוֹרוֹת עַל הָעֲרָבִים.
pages.source: תהילים קלז, ב ("עַל עֲרָבִים בְּתוֹכָהּ תָּלִינוּ כִּנֹּרוֹתֵינוּ"); ירמיהו כט, י; דברי הימים ב לו, כא
pages.illustration: CLOSE-UP. Color-script: night-blue, still. A single slender poplar branch crosses the page diagonally from upper-right to lower-left; from it hang three ancient lyres (asymmetric Near-Eastern kinnor shape, wooden arms, 7-10 strings), motionless, strings slack, one lyre slightly dusty with a spider-silk thread catching moonlight. Far below, a sliver of dark water. Yud: perched on the crossbar of the middle lyre, 9-10% height, eyes half-closed and flat (patient, waiting a very long time). Seventy years suggested visually, without numbers: willow leaves drifting, a faint pattern of many tiny moons repeating across the sky in a gold-line band (time passing) - decorative, not symbolic. The 'point of light' = one moonlit glint on a single string. Empty text-space: lower-right 40%, plain dark gouache. Mood: silence you can see. AVOID: musical notes, lyre shaped like a Greek harp or Irish harp, any figures, no text, no letters, no writing, no numerals, no idols or statues, no winged disc, no Marduk dragon (mushhushshu), no eight-pointed Ishtar star, no lamassu, no Eye of Horus, no ankh, no scarab, no depiction of God or divine figures, no beams-from-heaven cliché, no domes, no minarets, no turbans-with-jewels 'Arabian nights' costume, no pharaoh costumes, no bare shoulders or immodest dress, no photorealism, no 3D render, no glossy gradients.
pages.page_turn: השקט הכי עמוק - ואז, בדף הבא, משהו זז.

pages.source: עזרא א, א; דברי הימים ב לו, כב ("הֵעִיר ה'" - רמז חזותי בלבד, בלי ציור של הקב"ה)
pages.illustration: WORDLESS SPREAD, WIDE. The turning point. Color-script: night-blue, but with the FIRST warmth: a breath of pale gold enters from the RIGHT edge. A night wind sweeps across the whole scene, drawn as long elegant gouache ribbons of lighter blue edged with the finest gold line, flowing from right to left through the poplars; every leaf turns, the canal ripples in rhythmic graphic waves, a goat-hair tent flap lifts, a clay-lamp flame leans sideways. The hanging lyres from the previous page swing, and one string vibrates - shown as a soft gold shimmer, the 'point of light' grows into a small star of light on it. Yud: on the swinging lyre, mid-left, 7% height, eyes wide open, perfect circles (startled awake, alert). Sleeping exiles under blankets in the low foreground just begin to stir (a child sitting up, looking at the sky). Palm-arch on the horizon now catches a sliver of gold. No source of the wind is shown: no figure, no face in clouds, no hand, no beam from heaven - only the stirring itself. Empty text-space: none needed (wordless), but keep the upper-left quiet for breathing room. AVOID: storm/danger mood, lightning, faces in the wind, no text, no letters, no writing, no numerals, no idols or statues, no winged disc, no Marduk dragon (mushhushshu), no eight-pointed Ishtar star, no lamassu, no Eye of Horus, no ankh, no scarab, no depiction of God or divine figures, no beams-from-heaven cliché, no domes, no minarets, no turbans-with-jewels 'Arabian nights' costume, no pharaoh costumes, no bare shoulders or immodest dress, no photorealism, no 3D render, no glossy gradients.
pages.page_turn: דף בלי מילים: הילד שומע את הרוח בעצמו. בדפדוף - לאן הרוח הגיעה?

pages.text: הֵעִיר ה׳ אֶת רוּחַ כּוֹרֶשׁ מֶלֶךְ פָּרַס.
pages.source: דברי הימים ב לו, כב; עזרא א, א (ציטוט מדויק)
pages.illustration: WIDE, very high horizon, long view. Color-script: night-blue with the gold ribbon of wind now clearly golden. The wind-ribbon from the previous spread travels across a great dark plain (left to right is the past; here it flows toward the LEFT, forward) to a distant low Persian palace in the style of Pasargadae: a pillared hall with slender columns, a walled four-part garden ('pardes') with straight water channels and rows of cypress and palm. Only ONE window/doorway glows warm gold, and the ribbon of wind enters it. Cyrus is NOT shown - no figure, no silhouette; the lit opening is the whole story. Yud: riding the gold ribbon like a leaf, mid-page, 6-7% height, eyes curious (one slightly higher - wondering 'where are we going?'). Gold palmette-lotus band runs along the top of the palace wall. Empty text-space: lower 35%, dark plain. AVOID: Persepolis bull capitals (later period), winged disc above the palace, guards with spears foregrounded, any king portrait, no text, no letters, no writing, no numerals, no idols or statues, no winged disc, no Marduk dragon (mushhushshu), no eight-pointed Ishtar star, no lamassu, no Eye of Horus, no ankh, no scarab, no depiction of God or divine figures, no beams-from-heaven cliché, no domes, no minarets, no turbans-with-jewels 'Arabian nights' costume, no pharaoh costumes, no bare shoulders or immodest dress, no photorealism, no 3D render, no glossy gradients.
pages.page_turn: לילה וחלון אחד מואר - בדפדוף מתפרץ בוקר והזהב נכנס בגדול.

pages.text: "מִי בָכֶם מִכָּל עַמּוֹ, ה׳ אֱלֹהָיו עִמּוֹ, וְיָעַל!"
pages.source: דברי הימים ב לו, כג (ציטוט מדויק, סוף התנ"ך); "וַיַּעֲבֶר קוֹל בְּכָל מַלְכוּתוֹ וְגַם בְּמִכְתָּב" (לו, כב)
pages.illustration: WIDE, low horizon - the power of an empire's voice. Color-script: the FIRST BIG GOLD - dawn breaking over the night-blue city; sky in bands of ivory and mustard-glaze gold. In a plaza before a high wall of glazed lapis brick (palmette frieze only), a Persian herald stands on a low stepped platform: short belted coat, trousers, soft rounded felt cap, beard; he holds open a long blank scroll / leather roll edged with a gold palmette band. From the scroll, concentric arcs of fine gold line ripple outward across the whole page like sound. Below, a crowd of small Judean figures in profile frieze rows - wrapped headcloths, veils, long mantles - turning, lifting their heads; a child on a father's shoulders points. Yud: high on the top edge of the lapis wall at upper-right, 6% height, eyes huge and bright, leaning forward (she recognizes the sound). The 'point of light' = sunrise glint on the scroll's edge. Palm-arch: two palms frame the herald, their fronds now edged in gold. Empty text-space: upper-left 35% of pale dawn sky. AVOID: legible writing on the scroll, Cyrus Cylinder (it does not mention the Jews), the king himself, soldiers threatening, no text, no letters, no writing, no numerals, no idols or statues, no winged disc, no Marduk dragon (mushhushshu), no eight-pointed Ishtar star, no lamassu, no Eye of Horus, no ankh, no scarab, no depiction of God or divine figures, no beams-from-heaven cliché, no domes, no minarets, no turbans-with-jewels 'Arabian nights' costume, no pharaoh costumes, no bare shoulders or immodest dress, no photorealism, no 3D render, no glossy gradients.
pages.page_turn: הקריאה מסתיימת במילה אחת - ובדפדוף רואים מקרוב למי היא שייכת.

pages.source: דברי הימים ב לו, כג; עזרא א, ג ("וְיַעַל לִירוּשָׁלַיִם")
pages.illustration: CLOSE-UP, the emotional burst. Color-script: full warm gold, the first all-gold page. Plain luminous mustard-gold gouache field; the gold sound-arcs of the previous page now curl around Yud like ribbons. Yud: center-right, BIG (20-25% of image height), mid-jump, a few short gouache motion strokes beneath her tail, eyes as two upturned happy arcs (pure joy). Far in the background along the bottom, a tiny faint line-drawing of distant hills and a path climbing toward the LEFT (the road up), just a hint. Gold palmette-lotus band frames top and bottom. The white 'point of light' sits in the air just above her, like a spark she jumped toward. Empty text-space: upper-left 40%. AVOID: confetti, cartoon stars, any letters (the word itself is NOT drawn here), no text, no letters, no writing, no numerals, no idols or statues, no winged disc, no Marduk dragon (mushhushshu), no eight-pointed Ishtar star, no lamassu, no Eye of Horus, no ankh, no scarab, no depiction of God or divine figures, no beams-from-heaven cliché, no domes, no minarets, no turbans-with-jewels 'Arabian nights' costume, no pharaoh costumes, no bare shoulders or immodest dress, no photorealism, no 3D render, no glossy gradients.
pages.page_turn: מהרגש הגדול אל ההמולה: בדפדוף כולם אורזים.

pages.text: אָרְזוּ צְרוֹרוֹת. הַשְּׁכֵנִים הֵבִיאוּ כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב. וְהַגָּמָל, כְּמוֹ כָּל גָּמָל, רָטַן.
pages.source: עזרא א, ד ו-א, ו (השכנים נותנים כסף, זהב, רכוש ובהמה). הגמל הרוטן - ספרותי
pages.illustration: WIDE, busy but ordered courtyard, frieze-like. Color-script: transition from blue to terracotta - morning sun on sand and terracotta mud-brick walls, blue shadows still in the corners. Left to right a rhythm of small profile figures in modest dress: a grandmother pressing dates into a woven basket, a father knotting a cloth bundle, a boy rolling a reed mat, a goat-hair tent being folded; at the gate, neighbors who are staying (Babylonian-dressed, fringed robes) hand over a silver bowl and a small gold vessel and lead a donkey. Clay oil lamps and jars stacked on a mat. FOREGROUND RIGHT: a large flat terracotta camel with tasseled harness, kneeling, eyelids heavy, lower lip pushed out, one small puff of dust from its nostrils - unmistakably grumbling (comic anchor of the page). Yud: on top of the tallest bundle, center, 7% height, eyes squeezed into giggling arcs. Fairy-light lanterns strung along the wall; the 'point of light' = sunlight on the gold vessel. Empty text-space: top 35% band of pale sky above the wall. AVOID: the camel looking aggressive, mass of camels (camels were a minority), luxury treasure piles, no text, no letters, no writing, no numerals, no idols or statues, no winged disc, no Marduk dragon (mushhushshu), no eight-pointed Ishtar star, no lamassu, no Eye of Horus, no ankh, no scarab, no depiction of God or divine figures, no beams-from-heaven cliché, no domes, no minarets, no turbans-with-jewels 'Arabian nights' costume, no pharaoh costumes, no bare shoulders or immodest dress, no photorealism, no 3D render, no glossy gradients.
pages.page_turn: כסף וזהב של השכנים - ובדפדוף זהב אחר לגמרי, שחוזר הביתה.

pages.text: גַּם כְּלֵי בֵּית ה׳ יָצְאוּ מֵהָאוֹצָר — חוֹזְרִים הַבַּיְתָה.
pages.source: עזרא א, ז–יא (כורש מוציא את הכלים, מתרדת הגזבר סופר אותם לששבצר) - פשט, בלי מספר כלים
pages.illustration: MEDIUM-WIDE, ceremonial and calm. Color-script: terracotta and warm sand with gold highlights. A treasury doorway of mud brick with a glazed palmette border opens onto daylight; a Persian treasurer (short coat, soft cap, tablet and stylus or wax board - no visible writing) stands counting as Judean porters carry out vessels in a slow procession moving toward the LEFT: simple shallow gold and silver basins and bowls, plain ladles, lidded jars, carried in both hands or on padded cloths, each one glinting. A Judean elder (wrapped headcloth, long mantle) receives them with care. Keep the vessels simple and generic; NO menorah, no ark, no altar, no showbread table (not in the Ezra list; avoid identifying Temple furniture). Yud: reflected and sitting in the bowl of the nearest gold basin at lower-right, 7% height, eyes soft and wide (wonder - 'they are going home too'). The 'point of light' = a gleam on a basin rim. Empty text-space: upper 35% wall area in plain ivory. AVOID: a count of objects that reads as a number, Belshazzar feast imagery, treasure-chest pirate cliché, no text, no letters, no writing, no numerals, no idols or statues, no winged disc, no Marduk dragon (mushhushshu), no eight-pointed Ishtar star, no lamassu, no Eye of Horus, no ankh, no scarab, no depiction of God or divine figures, no beams-from-heaven cliché, no domes, no minarets, no turbans-with-jewels 'Arabian nights' costume, no pharaoh costumes, no bare shoulders or immodest dress, no photorealism, no 3D render, no glossy gradients.
pages.page_turn: מכמה כלים - אל כמות שאי אפשר לספור: בדפדוף, החמורים.

pages.text: חֲמוֹרִים: שֵׁשֶׁת אֲלָפִים שְׁבַע מֵאוֹת וְעֶשְׂרִים! יוּד הִתְבַּלְבְּלָה בַּחֲמוֹר הַשְּׁלֹשִׁים.
pages.source: עזרא ב, סז ("חֲמֹרִים שֵׁשֶׁת אֲלָפִים שְׁבַע מֵאוֹת וְעֶשְׂרִים"); נחמיה ז, סח
pages.illustration: EXTREME WIDE, high horizon - the comic scale page. Color-script: terracotta and sand road, pale turquoise sky. The caravan sets out: an endless Egyptian-relief frieze of small grey donkeys, rows upon rows receding in zigzag bands to the horizon, all walking toward the LEFT, each with a different geometric saddle-blanket (terracotta, rose, lapis, olive); families walking beside them, a few horses and mules, and only an occasional camel (camels are the minority). Bundles, tent poles, lyres now strapped on and travelling. Yud: on a rock at lower-right, 7% height, her two eyes drawn as tiny spirals (dizzy), a little orbit of three gold dots circling her head. The 'point of light' = one donkey in the far rows wears a tiny white bead - a 'find it' game. Empty text-space: upper 35% sky. AVOID: horses or camels dominating, real numerals or tally marks, no text, no letters, no writing, no numerals, no idols or statues, no winged disc, no Marduk dragon (mushhushshu), no eight-pointed Ishtar star, no lamassu, no Eye of Horus, no ankh, no scarab, no depiction of God or divine figures, no beams-from-heaven cliché, no domes, no minarets, no turbans-with-jewels 'Arabian nights' costume, no pharaoh costumes, no bare shoulders or immodest dress, no photorealism, no 3D render, no glossy gradients.
pages.page_turn: מהמון עצום - אל אחת קטנה: בדפדוף, ילדה אחת בתוך השיירה.

pages.text: יַלְדָּה קְטַנָּה שָׁאֲלָה: "גַּם אֲנִי? אֲנִי עוֹד קְטַנָּה." "גַּם אַתְּ."
pages.source: דברי הימים ב לו, כג ("מִי בָכֶם מִכָּל עַמּוֹ" - ההזמנה לכל אחד); הדו-שיח ספרותי
pages.illustration: CLOSE, intimate, eye-level of a child. Color-script: warm terracotta and dusty rose, soft afternoon light. Plain sand ground and a big empty sky; a single palm-arch, gold-edged, frames the pair like a doorway. A mother (long sage mantle, veil over her hair, modest) kneels to the height of her small daughter (terracotta dress, short braid under a small headcloth, clutching a tiny cloth bundle). The mother's hand rests on the girl's head. Behind them, very soft and small, the caravan's legs and hooves passing (out of focus, a rhythm, not detail). Yud: on top of the girl's bundle, 8% height, her eyes tilted up toward the mother, gently shining (moved - she is small too). Girl and Yud echo each other in scale and pose. The 'point of light' = a bead on the girl's bundle string. Empty text-space: upper 40% of plain sky. AVOID: sentimental tears, modern clothing, no text, no letters, no writing, no numerals, no idols or statues, no winged disc, no Marduk dragon (mushhushshu), no eight-pointed Ishtar star, no lamassu, no Eye of Horus, no ankh, no scarab, no depiction of God or divine figures, no beams-from-heaven cliché, no domes, no minarets, no turbans-with-jewels 'Arabian nights' costume, no pharaoh costumes, no bare shoulders or immodest dress, no photorealism, no 3D render, no glossy gradients.
pages.page_turn: "גם את" - ובדפדוף יוד מבינה שזה נכון גם לגבי עצמה.

pages.text: בְּלִי יוּד: "וְעַל". וְעַל מָה? עִם יוּד: "וְיָעַל"! מִישֶׁהוּ עוֹלֶה!
pages.source: דברי הימים ב לו, כג. משחק לשון של המחבר (לא מדרש): "וְיָעַל" = שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה
pages.illustration: GRAPHIC LAYOUT PAGE - the only page with real letters, which are composited later in HTML/SVG. The AI generates ONLY the background and Yud with EMPTY LETTER SLOTS. Color-script: split - left half muted dusty rose and flat (stillness), right half warm gold (motion). Layout: two horizontal rows of large blank rounded slots (soft paper-cut shapes, no letterforms). Top-left row: three slots in muted rose with a conspicuous EMPTY gap where one small slot is missing. Right side / bottom row: four slots glowing gold, and in the second-from-right position Yud herself fills the gap (12-15% height), eyes as happy arcs. Behind the right half, a stylized staircase of dunes climbing to the LEFT (going up); behind the left half, flat ground. Gold palmette-lotus band divides the two halves vertically. pages.text: הַשַּׁיָּרָה עָלְתָה קָדִימָה. וְיוּד שָׁאֲלָה: "אִם אֲנִי בַּסּוֹף... מָה יֵשׁ בַּהַתְחָלָה?"
pages.source: עזרא ב, א; ב, ע (העולים יוצאים לדרך). שאלת יוד - הרעיון של הסדרה
pages.illustration: WIDE, sunset, long road. Color-script: terracotta into rose and first dawn-gold at the horizon. The caravan as a long thin line of silhouettes winding away to the LEFT over the dunes toward distant pale hills; the grumbling camel is visible near the end, still sulking but walking (silent callback); the little girl turns back and waves. Yud: on a dune crest at lower-RIGHT, 7% height, facing the OPPOSITE way - toward the right edge - looking back across the land, which dissolves into a soft glowing haze at the far right horizon (the mysterious beginning). Her eyes: one round, one slightly raised - a question. A tiny white 'point of light' glimmers in that faraway right-hand haze, the first time it appears far away instead of near her. Palm-arch: a gold palm-arch stands alone on the right horizon like a gate. Empty text-space: upper 35% of banded sunset sky. pages.text: "אֲנִי אֶעֱלֶה," אָמְרָה יוּד, "אֲבָל אֲחוֹרָה — עַד הַהַתְחָלָה!"
pages.source: משחק על "וְיָעַל" (דברי הימים ב לו, כג) - החלטת יוד, ספרותי
pages.illustration: CLOSE-MEDIUM, decisive. Color-script: dawn gold rising behind blue-violet dunes. Yud: center-right, 14-16% height, turned toward the RIGHT edge (backward through the book), her tail lifted high and curled in a farewell wave toward the LEFT where, small and distant, the girl and her mother wave back from the end of the caravan. Yud's eyes are slightly narrowed and steady (determined, brave), with a tiny gleam of excitement. Her shadow stretches long to the left. At her feet the sand shows faint wave-like rows - the first hint that the land itself is made of lines of a scroll. The 'point of light' = the morning star above the right horizon. Empty text-space: upper-left 40%. pages.text: בֵּין הַשּׁוּרוֹת הִבְהֵב חוּט זָהָב. יוּד אָחֲזָה בּוֹ בַּזָּנָב — וְטִפְּסָה.
pages.source: חוט הזהב - אמצעי המסע של הסדרה (ספרותי, ללא מקור)
pages.illustration: WIDE, the world turns back into the scroll. Color-script: golden dawn, ivory paper glowing, lapis shadows. The desert dunes of the previous pages morph seamlessly into the rows of the great scroll (abstract ivory dashes, no letters) - the landscape IS the book. A single fine luminous gold thread winds between the rows from LEFT to RIGHT and upward, like a vine with tiny gold lotus buds, sparkling with fairy-light where it bends. Yud: holding the thread with her curled tail, climbing up-and-right, mid-page, 8% height, eyes bright and focused (adventure), a short trail of tiny gold dots behind her. Far down at the lower-left, the tiny caravan still visible on the last row, going the other way. The 'point of light' = the gleam at the thread's highest visible point. Gold palmette-lotus band along the bottom. Empty text-space: upper-left 35%. pages.text: טַק... טַק... טַק... מִי בּוֹנֶה שָׁם?
pages.source: רמז לפרק 2: נחמיה ב, יז ("לְכוּ וְנִבְנֶה אֶת חוֹמַת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם"); עזרא ג (התחלת הבנייה)
pages.illustration: WIDE, final hook, dawn over Jerusalem's hills. Color-script: full golden dawn over pale limestone, with grey-ochre ruins. The gold thread runs off the RIGHT edge of the page; right at that edge rises the corner of a broken city wall of large pale Judean limestone blocks with olive trees and grasses in the cracks, the Kidron valley and Mount of Olives as soft flat shapes beyond (no Temple, no domes). One block hangs in mid-air being lowered (only a rope and the stone - the builders are just off-page). In the wall, low and near the thread, a single small empty gap exactly the size and silhouette of Yud, with a warm light behind it. A few fine gold zigzag 'tak' marks and puffs of stone dust beside the blocks (graphic, not letters). Yud: on the thread just left of the gap, 8% height, turned three-quarters back toward the reader, eyes one round and one in a happy arc (curious invitation - turn the page). The 'point of light' shines through the Yud-shaped gap. Palm-arch: a single palm on the hill, fully gold. Empty text-space: upper-left 40% sky. teaser: בַּפֶּרֶק הַבָּא: חוֹמָה שְׁבוּרָה, הַרְבֵּה יָדַיִם, וְקוֹל אֶחָד: "לְכוּ וְנִבְנֶה!" וּבַחוֹמָה — חוֹר קָטָן אֶחָד, בְּדִיּוּק בַּגֹּדֶל שֶׁל יוּד.
questions: יוּד שָׁאֲלָה: "מָה יֵשׁ בַּהַתְחָלָה?" מָה אַתֶּם חוֹשְׁבִים שֶׁהִיא תִּמְצָא?
הַיַּלְדָּה שָׁאֲלָה: "גַּם אֲנִי?" מָתַי הִרְגַּשְׁתֶּם קְטַנִּים — וְגִלִּיתֶם שֶׁגַּם אַתֶּם חֲשׁוּבִים?
מָה הֱיִיתֶם אוֹרְזִים בַּצְּרוֹר לַדֶּרֶךְ הָאֲרֻכָּה לִירוּשָׁלַיִם?

nextChapters.anchor: מגילת אסתר — שם ה׳ אינו מופיע במגילה, ובכל זאת הנס נמצא בה. ״אסתר מן התורה מנין? ׳וְאָנֹכִי הַסְתֵּר אַסְתִּיר פָּנַי׳״ (חולין קלט ע״ב, על דברים לא, יח). הדבר הקטן: מה שנסתר.

sourcesNotes: הערות להורים ולמחנכים (לא חלק מטקסט הילדים). [פשט] (1) המילה האחרונה: "כֹּה אָמַר כּוֹרֶשׁ מֶלֶךְ פָּרַס... מִי בָכֶם מִכָּל עַמּוֹ, ה׳ אֱלֹהָיו עִמּוֹ, וְיָעַל" (דברי הימים ב לו, כג). הספר נגמר באמצע משפט, בלי "לִירוּשָׁלַיִם"; ההמשך בעזרא א, ג: "וְיַעַל לִירוּשָׁלַיִם אֲשֶׁר בִּיהוּדָה, וְיִבֶן אֶת בֵּית ה׳". עמוד 6 מצטט את הפסוק כלשונו. (2) סדר הספרים: לפי בבא בתרא יד ע"ב דברי הימים חותם את הכתובים, וכך בדפוסים. בכתר ארם צובא ובכתב יד לנינגרד הוא פותח את הכתובים. "המילה האחרונה" היא אפוא קריאה ספרותית לפי סדר הגמרא והדפוסים. (3) הגלות: "עַל נַהֲרוֹת בָּבֶל..." ו"עַל עֲרָבִים בְּתוֹכָהּ תָּלִינוּ כִּנֹּרוֹתֵינוּ" (תהילים קלז, א–ב; עמודים 2–3). "שבעים שנה" - ירמיהו כט, י ודברי הימים ב לו, כא, ו"לִכְלוֹת דְּבַר ה׳ בְּפִי יִרְמְיָהוּ" (לו, כב). (4) "הֵעִיר ה׳ אֶת רוּחַ כּוֹרֶשׁ" (דברי הימים ב לו, כב; עזרא א, א; עמוד 5). העמוד בלי המילים (עמוד 4) מציג רוח נושבת: זו פרשנות חזותית של המחבר למילה "רוּחַ" (רוח ונשמה), לא מדרש. הקב"ה אינו מצויר, וגם כורש אינו מצויר - רק חלון מואר ושליחו. "וַיַּעֲבֶר קוֹל בְּכָל מַלְכוּתוֹ וְגַם בְּמִכְתָּב" (לו, כב) הוא הבסיס לכרוז בעמוד 6. (5) השכנים נותנים "בְּכֶסֶף וּבְזָהָב וּבִרְכוּשׁ וּבִבְהֵמָה" (עזרא א, ד; א, ו; עמוד 8). לא כל העם עלה; מי שנשארו קיבלו מירמיהו הוראה "בְּנוּ בָתִּים" ו"דִּרְשׁוּ אֶת שְׁלוֹם הָעִיר" (ירמיהו כט, ה–ז), ואין בספר ביקורת עליהם. (6) כלי בית ה׳: כורש מוציא אותם, ומתרדת הגזבר סופר אותם לששבצר (עזרא א, ז–יא; עמוד 9). הסכום בפסוק (5,400) אינו תואם את הרשימה (2,499) - קושי ידוע, ולכן אין בספר מספר כלים. הרשימה כוללת קערות, אגרטלים ומחלפים; לכן באיור אין מנורה או כלים מזוהים אחרים. ששבצר וזרובבל - אדם אחד לפי סנהדרין לח ע"א. (7) המספרים (עמוד 10) מדויקים: "חֲמֹרִים שֵׁשֶׁת אֲלָפִים שְׁבַע מֵאוֹת וְעֶשְׂרִים" (עזרא ב, סז; נחמיה ז, סח). שם גם 736 סוסים, 245 פרדים ו-435 גמלים, וכל הקהל 42,360 (עזרא ב, סד–סו). לכן באיור רוב השיירה חמורים. (8) "מִי בָכֶם מִכָּל עַמּוֹ" - ההזמנה לכל אחד; הדו-שיח בין הילדה לאמה (עמוד 11) ספרותי. [דקדוק ומשחק לשון - של המחבר, לא מדרש] (9) "וְיָעַל" היא צורה מקוצרת של "יַעֲלֶה" ("וְשֶׁיַּעֲלֶה"). היו"ד היא אות העתיד שהופכת את המילה לעלייה; בלעדיה נשאר "וְעַל" (עמוד 12). [מדרש וחז"ל] (10) מגילה יב ע"א (לאמת): הקב"ה "קובל" על כורש שאמר רק "וְיָעַל" והשאיר את הבנייה לאחרים - רקע לחור בחומה ולפרק 2. (11) יומא ט ע"ב ("אילו עשיתם עצמכם כחומה") - מדרש על מי שלא עלו, להורים בלבד. (12) על חשיבותה של יו"ד אחת: שיר השירים רבה ה, יא; ויקרא רבה יט, ב. היו"ד של שָׂרַי שניתנה ליְהוֹשֻׁעַ: ירושלמי סנהדרין ב, ו (פרקים 19 ו-24). [ספרותי] (13) חוט הזהב, הגמל הרוטן, הסבתא והתמרים - פרטי סיפור. (14) רגע הזקנים הבוכים והצעירים המריעים (עזרא ג, יב–יג) קורה אחרי הנחת היסוד, ולכן נשמר לפרק 2. תהילים קכו ("שִׁיר הַמַּעֲלוֹת... הָיִינוּ כְּחֹלְמִים") - הקשר בין "מַעֲלוֹת" ל"וְיָעַל" מוצע לשיחה. הערה: "ה׳" בטקסט נקרא "הַשֵּׁם". אין בספר דיבור חדש בשם הקב"ה.
